# AmigaChrome Game Ports


**[Unified Port Atlas](https://github.com/DalsinAI/amigachrome/tree/main/docs/porting)** — searchable cross-programme game/application catalogue with existing Amiga-port evidence, source/rights assessment and proposed Open-family acceleration or development benefit. This does not replace the local source pins, build notes or qualification gates.

Open-source game-port and compatibility work for **m68k AROS**, **AmigaOS 3.x** and **AmigaChrome**.

The repository contains compiled revival ports, the Neverball/OpenGPU release lane, and the next 3D source-intake targets. Compile success is useful evidence, but it is **not** synonymous with release readiness. See [RELEASE_POLICY.md](RELEASE_POLICY.md).

## Live programme - 24 October 2026

The [live execution order and SDL3 intake](PORT_BACKLOG.md#live-execution-order---24-october-2026)
accept the reviewed games, applications and lab targets into the programme.
Finish the existing playable/SDL3 ports first. With OpenAL nearing readiness,
prepare its AC090 qualification and AstroMenace as the first consumer; availability
and audio success remain explicit gates. See the [full SDL3 review](docs/SDL3_PORT_REVIEW_20261024.md).
New intake entries still need audited source pins before becoming fetch/build targets.

## Post-merge checks - 13 October 2026

The port/SDL changes are merged and rebuilt. A new Amiga-only OpenJazz
configuration-directory check fixes the demonstrated false "not writable"
result. Chocolate Doom reached software-rendered gameplay, saved/loaded a
slot and exited 0 with sound explicitly disabled. Final OpenJazz startup/focus
repetition and Doom audio remain open, not release passes.

[Exact results, hashes, limits and next checks](evidence/postmerge-20261013/README.md).

## Latest verified state - dependency isolation and recovered text input

- **Fresh build work:** the affected recipes now require a locked codec inventory
  inside the selected stove. Both AssaultCube targets were rebuilt from a new
  exact-pinned checkout without the old WebKit include/library fallback.
- **Recovered earlier runtime evidence:** the PR67 SDL2 candidate delivered real
  shared/static ASCII text. Neverball accepted `DALEX`, Backspace made `DALE`,
  and the player name persisted across exit/relaunch. This is the candidate in
  the isolated lab, not an upstream merge or a production deployment.
- **SDLPoP:** a new `SDL_OPENGPU=0` lab run rendered Level 1, quicksaved,
  moved, quickloaded back to the saved position and returned exit 0. This is
  one bounded emulated-68040/software-mode check, not a complete release.

[Build/review receipts](evidence/open2-20261013-resume/README.md) and
[recovered runtime evidence](evidence/sdltext-20261012-recovered/README.md)
retain the source identities, hashes, raw output and remaining limitations.
No port has been promoted to RELEASE.

### Rendering qualification lanes

| Lane | Ports | Required additional gate |

| Plain 68040 + FPU / software 2D | OpenJazz, SDLPoP, Chocolate Doom | Run on the intended SDL CPU path with `SDL_OPENGPU=0`, plus input/audio/save/exit tests. This is a requirement, not a completed pass for all three. |
| OpenGPU-dependent 3D client | AssaultCube client; Neverball/Neverputt GL lane | Qualify the chosen supported OpenGPU backend. No plain-68040 performance claim. |
| No rendering | AssaultCube dedicated server | Socket/listen/stop tests, with the guest library version recorded. |

## Historical Open2 follow-up - actual guest first light

NXEngine-evo completed its Open2 link, and Neverball/Neverputt now rebuild and
pass the package gate. AssaultCube has two targeted fixes: one Amiga definition
for stream virtuals, and correct array deletion in game-mode parsing. The
previous duplicate stream-section and mismatched-delete diagnostics are absent
from the resulting links; other warnings and the audio stub remain.

**Runtime evidence:** SDLPoP rendered its intro and a diagnostic Level 1; Neverball
rendered its title and Level 01 3D start scene. Both returned guest exit code 0
in a separate, muted, stopped-source lab. Sixteen host regression tests and a
21-check stream diagnostic in the AmigaOS guest passed. No full game release.
Native name typing in Neverball remained empty on the recorded existing SDL2
runtime; the on-screen keyboard was a workaround, not a text-input pass.

[Follow-up results, screenshots, hashes and remaining gates](evidence/open2-20261012-followup/README.md).

## Open2 compiler pass - 12 October 2026

The port queue has resumed with **OpenAmigaGCC 16.2.0-open2**. OpenJazz,
Chocolate Doom, SDLPoP and both AssaultCube executables have new compile/link
artifacts. NXEngine-evo's longer rebuild was still running at the evidence
snapshot. No new game runtime or release pass is claimed.

See [retained results and risks](evidence/open2-20261012/README.md) and
[Open2 build instructions](docs/OPEN2_BUILDING.md). The shared CMake toolchain
now honours `STOVE`, preventing an accidental fallback to an older compiler.
The OpenGPU SDK archives remain explicitly recorded reused dependencies.

See [PORT_STATUS.md](PORT_STATUS.md) and the individual files under `ports/` for exact source pins, hashes, content boundaries and test gates.

## Repository layout

- `scripts/` — source preparation, build orchestration and field-test staging code.
- `port-layer/acgame/` — AmigaChrome AGA presentation code, smoke test and unit tests.
- `port-layer/uqm/` — UQM AROS bootstrap patcher and port notes.
- `ports/*/` — per-port build recipes, patches, release notes and qualification gates.
- `toolchain/aros-local/` — the AROS m68k toolchain bootstrap recovered from the AmigaChrome worktree.
- `gameports/catalog.json` — exact upstream source pins and content policy.

See [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) for the rebuild path.

## Source preparation and network policy

Upstream engine source remains in the upstream repositories and is referenced by exact pinned revisions or archive hashes.

Source preparation is **offline by default**. Existing valid prepared sources and cached archives are reused locally. If preparation would require an external fetch, it stops unless the caller explicitly supplies `--allow-network` after approval. An existing build or preparation script is not permission to access the network.

Game data, ROMs, proprietary assets and local test caches are **not** part of this repository unless a port's upstream licence explicitly permits redistribution and the release recipe records that provenance.

## Status language

- **SOURCE PINNED** means the exact upstream input has been selected but no successful target build is claimed.
- **COMPILED** means the pinned source has produced the target m68k executable.
- **FIRST LIGHT** means the executable has launched on an AmigaChrome guest.
- **TESTING** means runtime qualification is underway and at least one required release gate remains open.
- **TESTED** means the stated graphics, input, audio, persistence and clean-exit gates have been exercised.
- **RELEASE** means the port has passed its complete release gates, package/provenance checks and clean-instance runtime qualification.

**DONE means RELEASE.** Compiled, First Light and Testing are intermediate states.

## Licence

AmigaChrome-authored glue, scripts and documentation are MIT licensed unless a file says otherwise. Upstream projects retain their own licences. Game data retains its own rights and is not redistributed unless its licence and the port's release policy permit it.

No upstream game engine source is committed here. Prepared sources live outside Git at their pinned revision. Binaries built from them remain subject to the upstream licence, including source-offer and notice obligations where applicable.

public _draw_sprite

leftclipped:
    dc.w 0

rightclipped:
    dc.w 0

topclipped:
    dc.w 0

bottomclipped:
    dc.w 0

empty_pixels_on_right:
    dc.w 0

additional_word_added:
    dc.w 0

skew:
    dc.w 0

masked:
    dc.w 0

sprite_jump_table:
    dc.l 0 ; should never be used
    dc.l draw_eight_line_chunks    ; 16 wide
    dc.l draw_four_line_chunks    ; 32 wide
    dc.l draw_two_line_chunks    ; 48 wide

_draw_sprite:


    ; inputs:

    ; a0 = source data address?
    ; a1 = screen buffer address
    ; a3 = desired xpos to the pixel
    ; a4 = (nothing)
    ; a5 = (nothing)
    ; a6 = (nothing)

    ; d0 = (nothing)
    ; d1 = number of 16 pixel blocks to be drawn
    ; d2 = xpos in increments of 16 pixels (e.g. 2 = 32 pixels)
    ; d3 = (d7 - d5) + 1
    ;   (number of lines to draw) WE SHOULD BE ABLE TO CALCULATE THIS HERE
    ; d4 = (mirror of d1) WE SHOULD BE ABLE TO TRANSFER THIS HERE
    ; d5 = top of sprite ypos
    ; d6 = d2 + d1
    ;   (starting point in increments of 16 pixels + number of 16 pixel blocks to be drawn)
    ; d7 = bottom of sprite ypos

    ; what i want to pass in:
    ; xpos (signed word)
    ; ypos (signed word)
    ; source data pointer (long)
    ; source data width (word)
    ; source data height (word)
    ; screen buffer pointer (long)
    ;
    ; THEN
    ; - d1 = (source data width) >> 4
    ; - d2 = (xpos >> 4)
    ; - d3 = (source data height)
    ; - d4 = d1
    ; - d5 = (ypos)
    ; - d6 = (d1 + d2)
    ; - d7 = (d5 + d3)
    ; - a0 = (source data pointer)
    ; - a1 = (screen buffer pointer)
    ; - a3 = (xpos)

    ; xpos = word at sp + 6
    ; ypos = word at sp + 8
    ; source_data = long at sp + 12
    ; source_data_width = word at sp + 18
    ; source_data_height = word at sp + 22
    ; screen_buffer = long at sp + 24

    move.l sp,a0
    movem.l d2-d7/a2-a6,-(sp)

    moveq.l #0,d1
    move.w 18(a0),d1 ; source_data_width
    asr.w #4,d1
    move.l d1,d4

    moveq.l #0,d2
    move.w 6(a0),d2 ; xpos
    move.l d2,a3
    asr.w #4,d2

    moveq.l #0,d3
    move.w 22(a0),d3 ; source_data_height

    moveq.l #0,d5
    move.w 10(a0),d5 ; ypos

    move.l d1,d6
    add.l d2,d6 

    move.l d5,d7
    add.l d3,d7
    tst.w d3
    beq alldone

    move.l 24(a0),a1 ; screen buffer
    move.w 30(a0),empty_pixels_on_right
    move.w 34(a0),masked

    move.l 12(a0),a0 ; source data pointer

    moveq     #0,d0
    move.w    d0,leftclipped
    move.w    d0,rightclipped
    move.w    d0,topclipped
    move.w    d0,bottomclipped
    move.w    d0,additional_word_added

    move.l a3,d0                       ; get desired xpos of scenery object
    and.l #$f,d0                       ; convert to skew value for blitter
    move.w d0,skew
    cmp.w empty_pixels_on_right,d0
    ble.s zeroskew

    ;beq.s zeroskew

    move.w d2,d0                       ; get starting position in blocks of 16 pixels
    add.w d4,d0                        ; add number of 16 pixel blocks to be drawn

    cmp.w #$14,d0                      ; will part of sprite be off right side if we add 16 pixels?
    bpl.s setrightclipped              ; if yes, don't add 16 pixels to the right side

    addq.w #1,d4                        ; add another 16 pixel block to account for skew
    move.w #1,additional_word_added
    bra.s zeroskew

setrightclipped:

    move.w    #$ffff,rightclipped

zeroskew:

    tst.w     d2                       ; set flags for d2
    bpl.s     label_7a32c              ; jump when no left clipping required
    tst.w     d6                       ; bytes to skip after each line
    bmi       alldone                  ; if negative, nothing to draw
    move.w    d2,d0
    moveq     #0,d2                    ; clip scenery against left (left endmask should be 0xffff)
                                       ; at this point, left endmask needs be to 0xffff
    move.w    #$ffff,leftclipped
    add.w     d0,d4
    add.w     d0,d0
    suba.w    d0,a0
    add.w     d0,d0
    add.w     d0,d0
    suba.w    d0,a0

label_7a32c:
    tst.w     d5                       ; do we need to clip the top of the sprite?
    bpl.s     label_7a348              ; if we take the jump, no need to clip the top
                                       ; at this point, top is being clipped
    tst.w     d7                       ; is the bottom of the sprite off screen too?
    bmi     alldone                  ; if so, nothing to draw

    move.w    d5,d0
    moveq     #0,d5
    add.w     d0,d3
    tst.w     d3
    beq alldone

    add.w     d0,d0
    muls.w    d1,d0
    suba.w    d0,a0
    add.w     d0,d0
    add.w     d0,d0
    suba.w    d0,a0

label_7a348:
    cmp.w     #$14,d6
    bmi.s     label_7a35e              ; something to do with clipping against right side of screen
    cmp.w     #$14,d2                  ; does sprite need clipping on right edge?
    bpl       alldone            ; something to do with clipping - if sprite is entirely off screen?
    move.w    d6,d0
    subi.w    #$14,d0
    sub.w     d0,d4                    ; this is chopping off the sprite on the right edge
    move.w    #$ffff,rightclipped

    ; sprite has been clipped on right edge
    ; so endmask3 needs to be $ffff

label_7a35e:
    cmp.w     #199,d7   ; clip against bottom of screen
    bls.s     label_7a374
    sub.w     #199,d7
    addq.w    #1,d7
    sub.w     d7,d3           ; cut the bottom off the sprite
    bls     alldone

label_7a374:
    move.w    d4,d6
    add.w     d6,d6
    subi.w    #$28,d6
    neg.w     d6
    move.w    d1,d7            ; d7 = d1
    sub.w     d4,d7            ; d7 = d1 - d4 (result: blocks of 16 pixels to skip after each line)

    move.w    d7,d0            ; ...
    add.w     d0,d0            ; ...
    add.w     d0,d0            ; ...
    add.w     d0,d7            ; ...
    add.w     d7,d7            ; d7 = d7 * 10 (final value for number of source bytes to skip after each line)

    asl.w     #2,d6            ; d6 = d6 * 4 (final value of destination bytes to skip after each line)

    add.w     d2,d2            ; d2 = d2 * 2
    move.w    d5,d0            ; begin expression...
    add.w     d0,d0            ; ...
    add.w     d0,d0            ; ...
    add.w     d0,d5            ; ...
    asl.w     #3,d5            ; ... d5 = d5 * 40
    add.w     d5,d2            ; begin expression...
    add.w     d2,d2            ; ...
    add.w     d2,d2            ; ...
    ;adda.w    d2,a2            ; ... d2 = (d2 * 8 [see 7a38c]) + d5 (d5 must the start of a line within logbase, so a multiple of 160)
                                                                              ; we set d5 to 0 and everything renders at the top line of the screen
    ;adda.l    a1,a2        ; add buffer location into a2?
    ;movea.l   a2,a1            ; transfer destination address into a1
    add.w     d2,a1
    tst.w     d4
    beq       alldone
 
    ; end of modified lotus code and start of new blitter code
    moveq.l #10,d5

    ; draw a roadside object
    ; a0 is source address
    ; a1 is destination address
    ; d3 is the lines to be drawn
    ; d4 is number of 16 pixel blocks to be drawn (= 8 words)
    ; - so if d4 = 1, we want to draw 16 pixels = 4 words = 8 bytes
    ; d6 is destination bytes to skip after each line
    ; d7 is source bytes to skip after each line

    lea $ffff8a38.w,a2
    lea $ffff8a24.w,a4
    lea $ffff8a32.w,a5
    lea $ffff8a3c.w,a6

    addq.l #8,d6               ; convert to value suitable for blitter
    add.w d5,d7               ; convert to value suitable for blitter | TODO: #10 for 4bpp and #8 for 3bpp

    move.w d5,($ffff8a20).w   ; source x increment | TODO: #10 for 4bpp and #8 for 3bpp
    move.w #8,($ffff8a2e).w    ; dest x increment
    move.w #$201,($ffff8a3a).w ; hop/op: read from source, source & destination

    move.l a3,d0               ; get desired xpos of scenery object
    and.w #$f,d0               ; convert to skew value for blitter

    move.w d0,d1
    ;beq.s nonfsr               ; if skew is zero, we can't use nfsr

    ;cmp.w #1,d4
    ;beq.s nonfsr

    ;tst.w rightclipped
    ;bne.s nonfsr

    ;add.w d5,d7               ; TODO: #10 for 4bpp, #8 for 3bpp
    ;or.b #$40,d1

;nonfsr:

    tst.w leftclipped
    beq.s nofxsr

    sub.w d5,d7     ; TODO: #10 for 4bpp, #8 for 3bpp
    sub.l d5,a0

    or.b #$80,d1

    cmp.w #1,d4
    bne.s nofxsr 

    ; when words to draw = 4 and leftclipped != 0, we need to set endmask1 from rightendmasks
    ; In the case of a one word line ENDMASK 1 is used (http://www.atari-wiki.com/index.php/Blitter_manual)
    ; this is a special case and could do with tidying up

    move.w d7,($ffff8a22).w             ; source y increment
    move.w d6,($ffff8a30).w             ; dest y increment
    move.w d4,($ffff8a36).w             ; xcount = number of 16 pixel blocks (one pass per bitplane)
    move.b d1,($ffff8a3d).w

    lea.l rightendmasks(pc),a3
    add.l d0,d0                         ; byte offset in mask lookup table
    move.w (a3,d0.w),d1
    move.w d1,($ffff8a28).w             ; endmask1
    bra.s blitterstart

nofxsr:

    move.w d7,($ffff8a22).w             ; source y increment
    move.w d6,($ffff8a30).w             ; dest y increment
    move.w d4,($ffff8a36).w             ; xcount = number of 16 pixel blocks (once pass per bitplane)
    move.b d1,($ffff8a3d).w

    add.l d0,d0                         ; byte offset in mask lookup table
    move.w #-1,($ffff8a2a).w            ; endmask2

    move.w leftclipped(pc),d1
    bne.s nocalcendmask1                ; branch if zero flag not set

    lea.l leftendmasks(pc),a3
    move.w (a3,d0.w),d1                 ; fetch value of endmask1

nocalcendmask1:
    move.w d1,($ffff8a28).w             ; endmask1

    move.w rightclipped(pc),d1
    bne.s nocalcendmask3                ; branch if zero flag not set

    tst.w additional_word_added
    bne.s normalendmask3

    ; how many pixels do we need to draw?
    ; (16 - empty_right_pixels) + skew

    ;lsr.w #1,d0

    move.w skew,d0
    move.w #15,d1
    sub.w empty_pixels_on_right,d1
    add.w d1,d0
    add.w d0,d0

    ;move.w (a3,d0.w),d1
    ;move.w d1,($ffff8a2c).w            ; endmask3

    ;move.w #$ffff,($ffff8a2c).w            ; endmask3

    bra.s applyendmask

normalendmask3:
    move.w skew,d0
    sub.w empty_pixels_on_right,d0
    add.w d0,d0

applyendmask:
    lea.l rightendmasks(pc),a3
    move.w (a3,d0.w),d1

nocalcendmask3:
    move.w d1,($ffff8a2c).w            ; endmask3

    ; we are now free to use d0, d6 and d4 for our own purposes
    ; looks like d0, d1 and d2 are also available to us

blitterstart:

    cmp.w #3,d4
    bgt draw_one_line_chunks

    lea sprite_jump_table(pc),a3
    move.w d4,d2
    add.w d2,d2
    add.w d2,d2
    move.l (a3,d2.w),a3
    jmp (a3)

;draw_all:
;    move.w #798,2+drawsceneryplane_jsr    ; jump address in unrolled blitter calling table
;    move.w d3,finalblit+2                 ; ycount
;    bra.s draw_now

draw_eight_line_chunks:
    lea eight_line_chunks_lookup(pc),a3
    move.w d3,d2
    and.w #7,d2
    move.b (a3,d2.w),d2
    move.w d2,finalblit+2

    move.w #798,d1
    subq.w #1,d3
    and.w #$f8,d3
    lsr.w #1,d3
    sub.w d3,d1
    move.w d1,2+drawsceneryplane_jsr    ; jump address in unrolled blitter calling table
    moveq.l #8,d1                       ; ycount
    bra.s draw_now

eight_line_chunks_lookup:
    dc.b 8
    dc.b 1
    dc.b 2
    dc.b 3
    dc.b 4
    dc.b 5
    dc.b 6
    dc.b 7

draw_four_line_chunks:
    lea four_line_chunks_lookup(pc),a3
    move.w d3,d2
    and.w #3,d2
    move.b (a3,d2.w),d2
    move.w d2,finalblit+2

    move.w #798,d1
    subq.w #1,d3
    and.w #$fc,d3
    sub.w d3,d1
    move.w d1,2+drawsceneryplane_jsr    ; jump address in unrolled blitter calling table
    moveq.l #4,d1                       ; ycount
    bra.s draw_now

four_line_chunks_lookup:
    dc.b 4
    dc.b 1
    dc.b 2
    dc.b 3

draw_two_line_chunks:
    lea two_line_chunks_lookup(pc),a3
    move.w d3,d2
    and.w #1,d2
    move.b (a3,d2.w),d2
    move.w d2,finalblit+2

    move.w #798,d1
    subq.w #1,d3
    and.w #$fe,d3
    add.w d3,d3
    sub.w d3,d1
    move.w d1,2+drawsceneryplane_jsr    ; jump address in unrolled blitter calling table
    moveq.l #2,d1                       ; ycount
    bra.s draw_now

two_line_chunks_lookup:
    dc.b 2
    dc.b 1

draw_one_line_chunks:
    move.w #802,d1                      ; size of unrolled blitter calling table plus 2
    lsl.w #2,d3                         ; one entry in the table is 4 bytes
    sub.w d3,d1                         ; generate value to be placed within modified bra instruction
    move.w d1,2+drawsceneryplane_jsr    ; jump address in unrolled blitter calling table
    moveq.l #1,d1                       ; ycount
    move.w d1,finalblit+2

draw_now:
    move.b #$c0,d6                      ; blitter start instruction

    tst.w masked
    beq.s colour_unmasked

    rept 3
    bsr.s drawsceneryplane
    addq.l #2,a1                        ; move to next bitplane
    endr
    bsr.s drawsceneryplane

    subq.l #6,a1                        ; move destination back to initial bitplane

    move.w #$0207,($ffff8a3a).w         ; hop/op: read from source, source | destination
    bra.s colour

colour_unmasked:
    move.w #$0203,($ffff8a3a).w         ; hop/op: read from source, solid colour

colour:
    addq.l #2,a0                        ; move source to next bitplane
    bsr.s drawsceneryplane
    addq.l #2,a1                        ; move destination to next bitplane
    addq.l #2,a0                        ; move source to next bitplane
    bsr.s drawsceneryplane
    addq.l #2,a1                        ; move destination to next bitplane
    addq.l #2,a0                        ; move source to next bitplane
    bsr.s drawsceneryplane

    ;cmp.w #10,d5
    ;bne.s alldone

    addq.l #2,a1                        ; move destination to next bitplane
    addq.l #2,a0                        ; move source to next bitplane
    bsr.s drawsceneryplane

alldone:
    ;nop
    ;bra.s alldone

    movem.l (sp)+,d2-d7/a2-a6

    rts

drawsceneryplane:
    move.l a0,(a4)             ; set source address
    move.l a1,(a5)             ; set destination

drawsceneryplane_jsr:
    bra drawsceneryplane_aft
    rept 199
    move.w d1,(a2)             ; ycount
    move.b d6,(a6)
    endr
finalblit:
    move.w #1,(a2)
    move.b d6,(a6)
drawsceneryplane_aft:
    rts

  --version       Show version information

Example:

```shell
$ PngToPi1 input.png output.pi1
```

import struct
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog, ttk

def debug_tos_relocation_gui():
    # Global storage for file data
    file_data = {
        'header': None,
        'relocation_entries': None,
    }

    def load_file():
        # Open file selector
        file_path = filedialog.askopenfilename(title="Select TOS File")
        if not file_path:
            print("No file selected.")
            return

        file_label.config(text=f"Current file: {file_path}")
        process_file(file_path)

    def save_file():
        # Check if there's data to save
        if not file_data['header'] or not file_data['relocation_entries']:
            print("No data to save.")
            return

        # Open file dialog to select the save location
        file_path = filedialog.asksaveasfilename(defaultextension=".txt", filetypes=[("Text Files", "*.txt")])
        if not file_path:
            print("No file selected for saving.")
            return

        # Get the header and relocation entries from the dictionary
        header_rows = file_data['header']
        relocation_entries = file_data['relocation_entries']

        # Open the file and write the header and relocation entries
        with open(file_path, 'w') as f:
            # Write the headers
            f.write("TOS File Header Information:\n")
            for row in header_rows:
                f.write(f"{row[0]:<25}: {row[1]}\n")

            f.write("\nRelocation Entries:\n")
            f.write(f"{'Index':<8}{'Byte Value':<15}{'Current Address':<20}{'Original Value':<20}{'Relocated Value':<20}{'Error':<25}\n")
            f.write("="*100 + "\n")

            # Write the relocation entries
            for entry in relocation_entries:
                f.write(f"{entry['index']:<8}{entry['byte_value']:<15}{entry['current_address']:<20}{entry['original_value']:<20}{entry['relocated_value']:<20}{entry['error']:<25}\n")

        print(f"File saved to {file_path}")

    def process_file(file_path):
        # Read the TOS file
        with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
            tos_data = f.read()

        # Unpack the TOS header
        header_fmt = '>H4L2H'
        header_size = struct.calcsize(header_fmt)
        if len(tos_data) < header_size:
            print("File too short to contain a valid header.")
            return
        header = tos_data[:header_size]
        unpacked_header = struct.unpack(header_fmt, header)
        magic_number = unpacked_header[0]
        text_length = unpacked_header[1]
        data_length = unpacked_header[2]
        bss_length = unpacked_header[3]
        symbol_table_length = unpacked_header[4]
        flag = unpacked_header[5]
        reserved = unpacked_header[6]

        # Verify the magic number
        if magic_number != 0x601a:
            print("Invalid magic number. Not a valid TOS file.")
            return

        # Compute the total program length
        total_length = text_length + data_length + symbol_table_length

        # Program start address in file
        program_start_offset = 0x1c
        program_end_offset = program_start_offset + total_length
        if len(tos_data) < program_end_offset:
            print("File too short. Incomplete data.")
            return

        # Assume base address is 0x10000
        base_address = 0x10000
        program_start = base_address + program_start_offset
        text_end = program_start + text_length
        data_end = text_end + data_length
        relocation_start = base_address + program_end_offset        

        # Get the relocation table
        relocation_table_offset = program_end_offset
        relocation_table = tos_data[relocation_table_offset:]
        relocation_table_index = 0

        # Read the offset to the first relocatable address
        if len(relocation_table) < 4:
            print("Relocation table too short.")
            return
        first_offset_bytes = relocation_table[:4]
        first_offset = struct.unpack('>L', first_offset_bytes)[0]
        relocation_table_index += 4

        # Initialize current relocation address
        current_reloc_address = base_address + first_offset
        reloc_file_offset = program_start_offset + (current_reloc_address - base_address)

        # Check if the relocation address is valid
        text_data_end_offset = program_start_offset + text_length + data_length
        if reloc_file_offset + 4 > text_data_end_offset:
            print(f"Error: Relocation address 0x{current_reloc_address:08x} is beyond text + data sections.")
            return

        # Read the original value
        original_value_bytes = tos_data[reloc_file_offset:reloc_file_offset+4]
        original_value = struct.unpack('>L', original_value_bytes)[0]
        relocated_value = original_value + base_address

        # Prepare relocation entries list
        relocation_entries = []

        # Add the first relocation entry
        relocation_entries.append({
            'index': 0,
            'byte_value': f"0x{first_offset:08x}",
            'current_address': f"0x{current_reloc_address:08x}",
            'original_value': f"0x{original_value:08x}",
            'relocated_value': f"0x{relocated_value:08x}",
            'error': ''
        })

        # Process the relocation table
        while relocation_table_index < len(relocation_table):
            byte_value = relocation_table[relocation_table_index]

            if byte_value == 0:
                # End of relocation table
                break
            elif byte_value == 1:
                # Jump 254 bytes
                current_reloc_address += 254
            else:
                current_reloc_address += byte_value
                error_message = ''
                # Check 16-bit alignment
                if current_reloc_address % 2 != 0:
                    error_message = f"Address 0x{current_reloc_address:08x} not 16-bit aligned."
                else:
                    # Compute file offset
                    reloc_file_offset = program_start_offset + (current_reloc_address - base_address)
                    if reloc_file_offset + 4 > text_data_end_offset:
                        error_message = f"Address 0x{current_reloc_address:08x} beyond text + data."
                    else:
                        # Read original value
                        original_value_bytes = tos_data[reloc_file_offset:reloc_file_offset+4]
                        original_value = struct.unpack('>L', original_value_bytes)[0]
                        relocated_value = original_value + base_address
                # Add to entries list
                relocation_entries.append({
                    'index': relocation_table_index,
                    'byte_value': f"{byte_value} (0x{byte_value:02x})",
                    'current_address': f"0x{current_reloc_address:08x}",
                    'original_value': f"0x{original_value:08x}" if not error_message else '',
                    'relocated_value': f"0x{relocated_value:08x}" if not error_message else '',
                    'error': error_message
                })

            # Move to next byte in relocation table
            relocation_table_index += 1

        # Clear the Treeview
        for item in tree.get_children():
            tree.delete(item)

        # Insert data into Treeview
        for entry in relocation_entries:
            tree.insert('', 'end', values=(
                entry['index'],
                entry['byte_value'],
                entry['current_address'],
                entry['original_value'],
                entry['relocated_value'],
                entry['error']
            ))

        # Update header information
        header_rows = [
            [f"Magic number: 0x{magic_number:04x}", f"Symbol table length: {symbol_table_length} bytes", f"Flag: 0x{flag:04x}", f"Reserved: 0x{reserved:04x}"],
            [f"Text length: {text_length} bytes", f"Data length: {data_length} bytes", f"BSS length: {bss_length} bytes"],
            [f"Program Start: 0x{program_start:08x}", f"Text End: 0x{text_end:08x}", f"Data End: 0x{data_end:08x}"],
            [f"Relocation Table: 0x{relocation_start:08x}", f"Entries: {len(relocation_entries)}", f"Errors: {len([entry for entry in relocation_entries if entry['error']])}"]
        ]

        # Clear old header info and update
        for widget in header_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()

        for row in header_rows:
            row_frame = tk.Frame(header_frame)
            row_frame.pack()
            for label_text in row:
                label = tk.Label(row_frame, text=label_text, padx=10)
                label.pack(fill='x', side='left', expand=True)

        # Store the header information
        file_data['header'] = [
            ["Magic number", f"0x{magic_number:04x}"],
            ["Text length", f"{text_length} bytes"],
            ["Data length", f"{data_length} bytes"],
            ["BSS length", f"{bss_length} bytes"],
            ["Symbol table length", f"{symbol_table_length} bytes"],
            ["Flag", f"0x{flag:04x}"],
            ["Reserved", f"0x{reserved:04x}"],
            ["Program Start", f"0x{program_start:08x}"],
            ["Text End", f"0x{text_end:08x}"],
            ["Data End", f"0x{data_end:08x}"],
            ["Relocation Table Start", f"0x{relocation_start:08x}"],
            ["Relocation Entries", f"{len(relocation_entries)}"],
            ["Errors", f"{len([entry for entry in relocation_entries if entry['error']])}"]
        ]

        # Store the relocation entries
        file_data['relocation_entries'] = relocation_entries

    # Create GUI window
    gui_root = tk.Tk()
    gui_root.title("TOS Relocation Debugger")

    # Top Frame for filename and Load button
    top_frame = tk.Frame(gui_root)
    top_frame.pack(pady=10)

    # Filename label
    file_label = tk.Label(top_frame, text="No file loaded")
    file_label.pack(side='left', padx=10)

    # Load button
    load_button = tk.Button(top_frame, text="Load", command=load_file)
    load_button.pack(side='left', padx=10)

    # Save button
    save_button = tk.Button(top_frame, text="Save", command=save_file)
    save_button.pack(side='left', padx=10)

    # Header Frame
    header_frame = tk.Frame(gui_root)
    header_frame.pack(pady=10)

    # Relocation Entries Frame
    entries_frame = tk.Frame(gui_root)
    entries_frame.pack(fill='both', expand=True)

    # Scrollbar
    scrollbar = tk.Scrollbar(entries_frame)
    scrollbar.pack(side='right', fill='y')

    # Treeview for relocation entries
    columns = ('index', 'byte_value', 'current_address', 'original_value', 'relocated_value', 'error')
    tree = ttk.Treeview(entries_frame, columns=columns, show='headings', yscrollcommand=scrollbar.set)
    tree.pack(fill='both', expand=True)
    scrollbar.config(command=tree.yview)

# BABA IS C64

## by Nick Bensema

In March 2019, Arvi "Hempuli" Teikari released a puzzle game called Baba Is You for PC, Mac, and Nintendo Switch. It's a game where you solve puzzles by pushing tiles around, some of which change the rules of the game and the properties of objects. Description doesn't do it justice; watch the [trailer on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U7MJljsoUSo "Baba Is You release trailer").

I loved the concept, and I loved the game, but somehow instead of having the itch to play it, I got the itch to copy it, using Commodore 64 BASIC.

I got farther than I expected, but don't expect to finish.

The game runs, and responds to cursor commands, but is too slow to
actually play unless it is compiled.  When it is compiled with 
Basic-BOSS, it is playable, but I haven't copied any good levels 
into it yet.  Currently there are five tutorial-grade levels.

## Supported features

* Eight object tiles: empty, Baba, rock, wall, flag, water, key, door
* Sixteen word tiles: all objects, properties, and "IS"
* Seven properties: YOU, WIN, STOP, PUSH, SHUT, OPEN, SINK, LOSE
* Screen parser understands
  * both horizontal and vertical sentences
  * NOUN IS NOUN
  * NOUN IS PROPERTY
* Cursor keys control any number of YOU tiles
* A tile may contain both a foreground object and a background object.
  (Text can only be a foreground object.)
* Win condition is YOU tile overlaps a WIN tile.
* Moving objects are stopped by STOP tiles
* PUSH tiles attempt to move in the same direction when moved upon.
* OPEN tiles combine with SHUT tiles to form an empty tile.
* SINK tiles combine with any other tile to form an empty tile.
* MELT tiles are destroyed when combined with a HOT tile, which remains.
* LOSE tiles destroy any YOU tiles that move onto them.
* Undo with "Z"
* Reset with "R"
* Level skip with "N"
* Poke into the level with "P"
* Edit the level graphically with "E"
* Dump current level into DATA statement with "D"
* Very trivial levels that are very hard to edit.

## Build instructions

I did most of my development in C64 BASIC, but wanted to be able to track source
code changes through GitHub.  You should be able to build the game from the text
source code file by just typing `make`, if you have these tools available:

* `petcat` for converting between ASCII and CBM BASIC.  It comes with VICE.
   https://vice-emu.sourceforge.io/
* `bbcompiler` for using BasicBOSS to compile to something that will run
  in real time on a Commodore 64.  You can compile it from source with GCC
  in the `bbcompiler-src` directory here:  https://github.com/mbergmann-sh/basicbossGUI/

There is a dev script called `devbaba` that will build `baba.prg` and run it with VICE.
If you edit the program and save it, it should back-port all the changes you made to
`baba.bas`, and recompile it to `baba-compiled.prg`.

# Related projects

I ported this effort to C, compatible with cc65.  It includes a 2x2 tile mode.
https://github.com/unbibium/baba-cc65

If you're interested in Baba demakes, try this Pico-8 version:
https://www.lexaloffle.com/bbs/?pid=149645

If you're interested in 8-bit Baba demakes specifically, try "Adam is Me"
for the Atari 8-bit, which is the same concept but has many differences: 
https://aim.atariscene.pl/

gorlik-totoro64-readme-md.text: # Totoro64 A Studio Ghibli inspired fan game for the Commodore 64 Help chu-totoro catch the acorns before the timer expires. Avoid the poison berries and catch the bonus apples. Single player and two player cooperative mode. Good for kids to learn coding while having fun. 'V', 'N' and left-shift or joystick in port 2 to play. In two player mode, the second player uses joystick in port 1. The game fits on a standard 16K Commdore 64 cartridge. Can be played with VICE or online at C64 Online if the real HW is not avaiable. # Building To build the game cc65, a GNU compatible make and zopfli are required. just type make to build. Type make test to build and invoke VICE to test the game. The makefile will build the PAL and NTSC version of the game automatically. There are a few compile time options in the totoro.h header file. #define STAGE_TIME 60 default time for the stages. Can be any number from 1 to 99 #define SPRITE_MESSAGES use sprites for most on screen messages #define MOVIE_TITLE use a font similar to the movie for the title screen The makefile will also build two slightly different layouts. The 'normal' layout uses a standard multicolor bitmap for the entire screen. The 'HIRES' layout uses a raster irq to split the screen in a non multicolor text mode area in the first 16 scanlines to display high resolution text. # Graphics editors Three different editors have been used for the artwork. VChar64 for the charset, cbm prg studio for the sprites and multipaint for the backgorund. # Implementation details Chu-totoro is made up of 3 layered sprites. Two single color for the black outline and the blue details. One multicolor to fill in the bag and the white belly. Chibi-totoro is made up of 2 single color layered sprites. One sprite is reserved for the spin top and potential additional game items. The two remaining sprites are used by the multiplexer to display up to 8 falling items. The music player is implemented using a custom IRQ player that is locked to VSYNC. The game has correction for PAL and NTSC timing for both playback speed and pitch. Most game assets are compressed to fit into the 16K cartridge limit. Decompression is done in the title screen using the cc65 zlib routines. In the hires game mode the IRQ to do split screen is not perfectly stable. A black line between the hires and the multicolor sections is used to hide the artifacts. In hires mode additional sprite multiplexing is used to display the icons in the status bar.

# c64SIDkit

SID chip sound effects toolkit for Commodore 64 game development.

![demo](demo/demo.gif)

## Features

- Python SID emulation with multiple backends: `sid_emulator.py`, `resid_emulator.py`, `vice_emulator.py`
- JSON-based SFX patch format with dataclass/schema validation in `schema.py`
- Built-in SFX preset library in `presets.py`
- WAV preview/export pipeline (`wav_export.py`)
- 6502 ASM export for C64 integration (`asm_export.py`)
- Command-line tool (`sid_sfx/cli.py`)
- Pygame SFX Tweaker GUI (`tools/sfx_tweaker.py`)
- Native C64 audition tool (`tools/sfx_audition.py` + `tools/sfx_audition.asm`)

## Installation

```bash
pip install .
```

Optional GUI dependencies (Pygame tools):

```bash
pip install '.[tools]'
```

## Quick Start

Render a built-in preset to WAV:

```bash
sid-sfx play fire
```

Render a patch JSON to WAV with a specific backend:

```bash
sid-sfx preview patches/powerup_speed.json --emulator resid --chip 8580 -o out/powerup_speed.wav
```

Export one or more patch JSON files to 6502 ASM:

```bash
sid-sfx export patches/xwing_blaster_filtered.json patches/tie_cannon_filtered.json -o out/sfx_data.asm
```

Export in separate table format:

```bash
sid-sfx export patches/xwing_blaster_filtered.json -f tables -o out/sfx_tables.asm
```

## SFX Tweaker

`tools/sfx_tweaker.py` is a real-time patch editor for rapid sound design iteration. It loads presets, lets you tweak waveform/envelope/frequency/sweep/filter/vibrato/loop parameters with sliders, and re-renders audio live via the SID renderer.

Key controls:
- `P`: play once
- `Space`: toggle auto-repeat
- `S`: print/save current patch (`patches/<name>.json`)
- `L`/`Right` and `Left`: cycle presets
- `R`: randomize parameters
- `N`: create a new preset

Run:

```bash
python tools/sfx_tweaker.py
```

Or start on a specific preset:

```bash
python tools/sfx_tweaker.py fire
```

## JSON Patch Format

Each patch is a JSON object mapping directly to SID-oriented parameters (`SfxPatch` in `schema.py`). Core fields include:

- Identity/voice: `name`, `voice`
- Oscillator: `waveform`, `freq_hi`, `freq_lo`, `pw_hi`
- Envelope: `attack`, `decay`, `sustain`, `release`
- Timing: `duration_frames`
- Optional modulation: `sweep_target_hi`, `sweep_target_lo`, `sweep_frames`, `sweep_type`, `vibrato_rate`, `vibrato_depth`
- Optional preview filter: `filter_mode`, `filter_cutoff`, `filter_resonance`
- Optional sustain behavior: `loop`, `loop_preview_seconds`

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "fire",
  "voice": 3,
  "waveform": "TRIANGLE",
  "freq_hi": 143,
  "freq_lo": 92,
  "attack": 8,
  "decay": 3,
  "sustain": 8,
  "release": 4,
  "pw_hi": 57,
  "duration_frames": 15,
  "sweep_target_hi": 14,
  "sweep_target_lo": 33,
  "sweep_frames": 13,
  "sweep_type": "exponential",
  "filter_mode": "lowpass",
  "filter_cutoff": 47,
  "filter_resonance": 5,
  "vibrato_rate": 0.0,
  "vibrato_depth": 0,
  "loop": false,
  "loop_preview_seconds": 5.0,
  "description": "Triangle sweep laser pew"
}
```

## Presets

Built-in presets (`sid-sfx play --list`):

- `fire`
- `explode`
- `hit`
- `weakpoint_hit`

# ACGame AGA/040 port layer

ACGame is the small common layer for AmigaChrome game ports targeting an AGA A1200-class machine with a 68040 and large Zorro III Fast RAM.

The first rule is architectural: Fast RAM is the workspace; Chip RAM is the presentation boundary. A large Z3 allocation does not make AGA DMA read Fast RAM.

## What is here

- `acgame_c2p8_ref` and `acgame_c2p8_fast`: 8-bit chunky to eight AGA-style
  bitplanes. The reference is simple and correct; the fast one gives the same
  bytes through an 8x8 bit transpose in 32-bit registers and is what the
  backend uses.
- `acgame_ham8_encode_row`: greedy RGB-to-HAM8 scanline encoder with a 64-colour base palette, plus a matching decoder for tests/offline tooling.
- The Amiga backend (`src/platform_aros_aga.c`, AmigaOS 3.x and AROS m68k):
  AGA or RTG 8-bit screens, keyboard, mouse, and pads through OpenInput with
  lowlevel.library as the fallback. See `AROS_AGA.md`.

Gameplay should normally use indexed 256-colour AGA. HAM8 is intended for title art, portraits, briefings, loading screens and other static or slowly changing presentation where horizontal dependency is acceptable.

This copy (amigachrome-guest `gameports/acgame/`) is the one the game ports
build from: amigachrome-gameports' `scripts/build_game_ports_job.py` and the
OpenOMF profile take ACGame from here. amigachrome-gameports
`port-layer/acgame/` holds the same files.

## Still to come

The platform layer is still to provide:

- 320x200, 320x240 and 320x256 indexed AGA surfaces;
- two Chip-RAM planar display buffers;
- Fast-RAM chunky render surfaces;
- HAM8 display setup and pre-encoded presentation frames;
- Paula-first audio with an optional AHI backend;
- timer and file wrappers suitable for AmigaOS 3.x and AROS 68k.

The backend opens AGA and RTG screens on OS 3.2.3 and reads pads through OpenInput (tested on an AmigaChrome lab instance, 9 October 2026). No claim is made yet that any of the four games links on 68k against this backend.


## Canonical copy

The canonical ACGame source currently lives in `DalsinAI/amigachrome-guest/gameports/acgame/`.
This copy is kept as a synchronized mirror for the game-ports repository. The Kitchen build job
and the OpenOMF AGA profile consume the guest copy at the pinned `GUEST_PORT_COMMIT`; changes
must land there first so the two trees do not become independent implementations.

# ACGame for AmigaOS 3.x with the os32-gcc16 stove (GCC 16.2 with the Team's
# fixes, libnix, the OpenGPU SDK 0.7).
#   make -f Makefile.amigaos STOVE=/path/to/stoves/os32-gcc16/prefix
#   make -f Makefile.amigaos CPU=-m68020  compatibility build
# The build must stay clean: -Werror, and no warning switched off.
STOVE   ?= $(HOME)/AmigaChrome/stoves/os32-gcc16/prefix
CC      = $(STOVE)/bin/m68k-amigaos-gcc
AR      = $(STOVE)/bin/m68k-amigaos-ar
CPU     = -m68040 -m68881
CFLAGS  = -noixemul -std=gnu99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks $(CPU) -Iinclude
LDFLAGS = -noixemul $(CPU)
BUILD   = build/amigaos

LIB_OBJS = $(BUILD)/c2p_ref.o $(BUILD)/ham8.o $(BUILD)/platform_aros_aga.o
PROGRAMS = $(BUILD)/acgame-aga-smoke $(BUILD)/acgame-rtg-smoke $(BUILD)/acgame-smoke $(BUILD)/acgame-joy

all: $(BUILD)/libacgame.a $(PROGRAMS)

$(BUILD)/libacgame.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(BUILD)/%.o: src/%.c include/acgame/*.h | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/smoke-aga.o: examples/aga_smoke.c include/acgame/*.h | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -DACGAME_SMOKE_DISPLAY=ACGAME_DISPLAY_AGA -c -o $@ $<
$(BUILD)/smoke-rtg.o: examples/aga_smoke.c include/acgame/*.h | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -DACGAME_SMOKE_DISPLAY=ACGAME_DISPLAY_RTG -c -o $@ $<
$(BUILD)/smoke-auto.o: examples/aga_smoke.c include/acgame/*.h | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<
$(BUILD)/joy_test.o: examples/joy_test.c include/acgame/*.h | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/acgame-aga-smoke: $(BUILD)/smoke-aga.o $(BUILD)/libacgame.a
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $^
$(BUILD)/acgame-rtg-smoke: $(BUILD)/smoke-rtg.o $(BUILD)/libacgame.a
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $^
$(BUILD)/acgame-smoke: $(BUILD)/smoke-auto.o $(BUILD)/libacgame.a
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $^
$(BUILD)/acgame-joy: $(BUILD)/joy_test.o $(BUILD)/libacgame.a
	$(CC) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ $^

	mkdir -p $@

	cmp #(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED | PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_ANIM_WITHIN_LOOP_REGION)
	bne !skip+
	player_set_state(PLAYER_STATE_CROUCH)
	!skip:

	input_fire()
	beq !fire_pressed+
	jmp !skip+
	!fire_pressed:
	player_set_state(PLAYER_STATE_ATTACK)
	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_WEAPON)
	beq !skip_jmp+
	jmp !skip+
	!skip_jmp:
	lda #0
	sta REG_WEAPON_PROPERTIES
	sprite_enable(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON)
	input_down()
	bne !skip_crouch_attack+
	set_sprite_pos_to_player(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, 4)
	jmp !skip+
	!skip_crouch_attack:
	set_sprite_pos_to_player(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, -5)
	!skip:

	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	and #(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED | PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_ANIM_WITHIN_LOOP_REGION)
	cmp #(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED | PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_ANIM_WITHIN_LOOP_REGION)
	bne !skip+
	player_set_state(PLAYER_STATE_IDLE)
	!skip:

	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED
	bne !skip+
	player_set_state(PLAYER_STATE_JUMP) // not really jump, this will be activated if falling
	!skip:

	!player_skip_alive:

	player_update()

	weapon_update()

	jsr update_enemies

	sprite_anim(SPRITE_ID_KEY_BLUE, REG_KEY_BLUE_FRAME, KEY_FRAME_START, KEY_FRAME_COUNT, %00000111, true, false, false)
	sprite_anim(SPRITE_ID_KEY_PURPLE, REG_KEY_PURPLE_FRAME, KEY_FRAME_START, KEY_FRAME_COUNT, %00000111, true, false, false)

	update_sprites_active()

	lda #PURPLE // overwrite the purple key specifically
	sta REG_SPRITE_COLOR + SPRITE_ID_KEY_PURPLE

	dbg_end()

	interrupt_end()
}

	sta REG_SPRITE_MULTICOLOR
	sta REG_SPRITE_PRIORITY

	ldx #0
	!:
	.for(var i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
		lda REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_COLOR_RAM + 250 * i,x
		sta REG_COLOR_RAM + 250 * i,x
	}
	inx
	cpx #250
	bne !-

	// Arok color RAM row (makes text white for whole scrolling row):
	lda #WHITE
	ldx #0
	!:
	sta REG_COLOR_RAM + 40 * 24,x
	sta REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SCREEN_RAM + 40 * 24,x
	inx
	cpx #40
	bne !-

	lda #picture.getBackgroundColor()
	sta REG_BACKGROUND_COLOR
	sta REG_BORDER_COLOR
	lda #%00000001 // VIC config bank 3: https://www.c64-wiki.com/wiki/VIC_bank
	sta $dd00
	lda #%00111011 // bitmap mode, screen visible
	sta $d011
	lda #%00011000 // multicolor mode
	sta $d016
	lda #%00001000 // screen mem, bitmap mem config
	sta $d018

	rand_init()

	// splash screen sprite setup:
	lda #255
	sta REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	.for(var i = 0; i < 8; i++)
	{
		lda #((REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SPRITE_DATA - SPLASH_SCREEN_VIC_BANK_BEGIN) / 64)
		sta REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SPRITE_PTR + i

		ldx #i
		rand()
		sta REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SPRITE_MOVEMENT_0,x

	sei           // Disable interrupts
	lda #$7f      // Disable CIA interrupts
	sta $dc0d
	sta $dd0d

	ora #$01
	sta $d01a

	cli           // Enable interrupts
	jmp *         // Infinite loop

splash_screen_update: {

	input_fire()
	bne !skip+
	jmp splash_screen_end
	!skip:

	dbg_begin(RED)

	// splash screen sprite anim:
	.for (var i = 0; i < 8; i++) {

		// Check movement re-roll:
		ldx #i
		rand()
		cmp #5 // re-roll chance
		bcs !+
		rand() // re-roll
		sta REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SPRITE_MOVEMENT_0,x
		!:

		// horizontal movement:
		lda REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SPRITE_MOVEMENT_0,x
		and #%00000001
		beq !+
		move_sprite_left(i, 1)
		jmp !next+
		!:
		move_sprite_right(i, 1)
		!next:
		wrap_sprite_hiposaware(i)

		// vertical movement:
		lda REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_SPRITE_MOVEMENT_0,x
		and #%00000010
		beq !+
		move_sprite_up(i, 1)
		jmp !next+
		!:
		move_sprite_down(i, 1)
		!next:
	}

	dbg_end()

	lda REG_SCREEN_CONTROL
	and #%11110000 // 38 col, h-scroll reset

	lda #50
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
	inc REG_GAME_FRAME_COUNTER
	lda REG_GAME_FRAME_COUNTER
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_HI

	interrupt_chain(splash_screen_wave, 50)
}
splash_screen_wave: {
	dbg_begin(GREEN)

	// apply sine value in horizontal scroll reg:
	lda REG_GAME_TEMP_HI
	and #63
	tax
	lda REG_SCREEN_CONTROL
	and #%11110000 // 38 col, h-scroll reset
	ora sineTable,x // add h-scroll
	sta REG_SCREEN_CONTROL
	inc REG_GAME_TEMP_HI

	// Jump some lines:
	lda REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
	clc
	adc #4
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
	
	dbg_end()

	lda REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
	cmp #240
	bcs !ret+

	// Chain next line:
	lda #<splash_screen_wave	// Set interrupt vector
	sta $0314
	lda #>splash_screen_wave
	sta $0315
	lda REG_GAME_TEMP_LO // line
	sta $d012
	lda $d011 	// Clear high bit of raster
	and #$7f
	sta $d011
	asl $d019 	// Acknowledge interrupt
	jmp $ea81	// jump into shorter ROM routine to only restore registers from the stack etc

	!ret:
	is_ntsc() // NTSC will skip the arok scroll, the timing for that is unfortunately too long on NTSC and interferes with next frame wave update
	beq !+
	interrupt_chain(splash_screen_arok, 241)
	!:
	interrupt_set(splash_screen_update, 30)
	asl $d019	// Acknowledge interrupt
	jmp $ea31	// Jump to system IRQ handler
}
splash_screen_arok: {

	lda REG_SCREEN_CONTROL
	and #%11110000 // 38 col, h-scroll reset
	sta REG_SCREEN_CONTROL

	lda REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	sec
	sbc #1
	and #%00000111
	sta REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	bne !+
	interrupt_chain(arok_memmove, 245)
	!:
	lda REG_SCREEN_CONTROL
	and #%11110000 // 38 col, h-scroll reset
	ora REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	sta REG_SCREEN_CONTROL

	interrupt_set(splash_screen_update, 30)
	asl $d019	// Acknowledge interrupt
	jmp $ea31	// Jump to system IRQ handler
}
arok_memmove: {
	// reset scroll immediately and move memory:
	dbg_begin(PURPLE)
	// wrap copy first block to end padded mem:
	.for(var i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
		lda REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_BITMAP_DATA + 40 * 8 * 24 + i
		sta REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_BITMAP_DATA + 40 * 8 * 25 + i
	}
	// memmove with wrapping:
	.for(var i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
		ldx #0
		!:
		lda REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_BITMAP_DATA + 40 * 8 * 24 + (i + 1) * 8,x
		sta REG_SPLASH_SCREEN_BITMAP_DATA + 40 * 8 * 24 + i * 8,x
		inx
		cpx #8
		bne !-
	}
	dbg_end()

	interrupt_set(splash_screen_update, 30)
	asl $d019	// Acknowledge interrupt
	jmp $ea31	// Jump to system IRQ handler
}

load_map_column_y: {
	lda #(REG_MAP_DATA & $FF)
	clc
	adc REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
	lda #(REG_MAP_DATA >> 8)
	adc REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_HI
	.for(var row = 1; row < 25; row++) {
		lda (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
		ldx #row
		jsr handle_map_item
		sta REG_SCREEN + row * 40, y
		tax
		lda REG_CHARSET_ATTRIBUTES,x
		sta REG_COLOR_RAM + row * 40, y

		.if(row < 24) { // last iteration doesn't need row memory bumping
			.if(MAP_WIDTH == 256) {
				// Specialized optimal way of bumping row offset when map is exactly 256 wide:
				inc REG_GAME_TEMP_HI
			}
			else {
				// Add MAP_WIDTH to tmp address:
				lda REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
				clc
				adc #(MAP_WIDTH & $FF)
				sta REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
				lda REG_GAME_TEMP_HI
				adc #(MAP_WIDTH >> 8)
				sta REG_GAME_TEMP_HI
			}
		}
	}
	rts
}

.macro update_scroll_reg() {
	// Sync the logical and hardware scroll regs:
	lda REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	and #%00000111
	sta REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL

	lda REG_SCREEN_CONTROL

scroll_map_left: {
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	cmp #((MAP_WIDTH - 38) & $FF)
	bne !can_scroll+
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	cmp #((MAP_WIDTH - 38) >> 8)
	bne !can_scroll+
	rts // No scroll above map bounds
	!can_scroll:

	dec REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL

	bpl !skip+
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	clc
	adc #1
	sta REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	adc #0
	sta REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	lda #(SCROLL_ATTRIBUTE_LEFT_PASS0 | SCROLL_ATTRIBUTE_LEFT_PASS1)
	sta REG_SCROLL_ATTRIBUTES
	!skip:

	update_scroll_reg()

	.for(var sprite_id = 0; sprite_id < 8; sprite_id++) {
		dec REG_SPRITE_X + sprite_id * 2
		bpl !skip+
		// hi-bit removal
		lda REG_SPRITE_H
		and #(~(1 << sprite_id))
		sta REG_SPRITE_H
		!skip:
	}

	rts

	lda REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	cmp #7
	bne !can_scroll+
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	cmp #0
	bne !can_scroll+
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	cmp #0
	bne !can_scroll+
	rts // No scroll below map bounds
	!can_scroll:

	inc REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL

	lda REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	and #%00000111

	bne !skip+
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	sec
	sbc #1
	sta REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_LO
	lda REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	sbc #0
	sta REG_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OFFSET_HI
	lda #(SCROLL_ATTRIBUTE_RIGHT_PASS0 | SCROLL_ATTRIBUTE_RIGHT_PASS1)
	sta REG_SCROLL_ATTRIBUTES
	!skip:

	update_scroll_reg()

	.for(var sprite_id = 0; sprite_id < 8; sprite_id++) {
		inc REG_SPRITE_X + sprite_id * 2
		bne !skip+
		// hi-bit add:
		lda REG_SPRITE_H
		ora #(1 << sprite_id)
		sta REG_SPRITE_H
		!skip:
	}

	rts
}

.macro spawn(idx) {
	sprite_enable(idx)

	// Row is taken at compile time
	//lda #((row + 2) * 8 + SCREEN_BORDER_Y_OFFSET - SPRITE_PIXEL_HEIGHT)
	// Row is taken from X register
	txa
	clc
	adc #2
	// row * 8:
	asl
	asl
	asl
	adc #(SCREEN_BORDER_Y_OFFSET - SPRITE_PIXEL_HEIGHT)
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + idx * 2

	// Column is taken from Y register
	cpy #(256 / 8)
	bcs !hi_pos+ // if A >= (256 / 8) -> hi-pos handling

	// lo-pos handling:
	lda #(~(1 << idx))
	and REG_SPRITE_H
	sta REG_SPRITE_H
	tya
	jmp !end+

	!hi_pos:
	lda #(1 << idx)
	ora REG_SPRITE_H
	sta REG_SPRITE_H
	tya
	sec
	sbc #(256 / 8) // row - (256 / 8)

	!end:
	// column * 8:
	asl
	asl
	asl
	clc
	adc #(SCREEN_BORDER_X_OFFSET + CHAR_PIXEL_SIZE / 2 - SPRITE_PIXEL_WIDTH / 2)
	adc REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + idx * 2
}
.macro set_sprite_pos(idx, posX, posY) {

		lda #(1 << idx)

		sta REG_SPRITE_H
		lda #(posX - 256)
	}
	else {
		// Normal 8 bit posX handling
		lda #(~(1 << idx))
		and REG_SPRITE_H
		sta REG_SPRITE_H
		lda #posX
	}
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + idx * 2
	lda #posY
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + idx * 2
}

	lda REG_SPRITE_X + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY * 2

	lda REG_SPRITE_Y + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY * 2

	.if(offsetY < 0) {
		sec
		sbc #-offsetY
	}
	.if(offsetY > 0) {
		clc
		adc #offsetY
	}

	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + idx * 2

	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY)
	bne !setbit+
	// unset bit
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(~(1 << idx))
	jmp !setbit_end+
	!setbit:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	ora #(1 << idx)
	!setbit_end:
	sta REG_SPRITE_H

	lda REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY)
	beq !noflip+
	// flip:
	lda REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
	ora #(1 << idx)
	jmp !skip+
	!noflip:
	lda REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
	and #(~(1 << idx))
	!skip:
	sta REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
}

move_player_right: {
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, 5, 14, true, false)
	cmp #208
	bcs !end+ // if A >= 208 -> stop move

	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY)
	beq !low+ // If and result is zero then high bit is not set, handle low byte case
	
	// Here is high-byte case:
	!high:

	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	jmp !end+

	// Here is low byte case:
	!low:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	cmp #(255 - PLAYER_MOVE_SPEED)
	bcs !overflow+ // handle overflow
	clc
	adc #PLAYER_MOVE_SPEED
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	cmp #(SCREEN_EXIT_LEFT + 120)
	bcc !skip_scroll+
	lda REG_GAME_FINISH
	bne !skip_scroll+
	jsr scroll_map_left
	!skip_scroll:
	jmp !end+

	!overflow:
	lda #0
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	ora #((1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY) | (1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR))
	sta REG_SPRITE_H

	!end:
	player_remove_flipped()

	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_RIGHT
	and #(~PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_LEFT)
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES

	and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED
	beq !skip+
	player_set_state(PLAYER_STATE_WALK)
	jsr sound_footstep
	!skip:

move_player_left: {
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, -5, 14, true, false)
	cmp #208

	// Check high bit:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H

	beq !low+ // If and result is zero then high bit is not set, handle low byte case
	
	// Here is high-byte case:
	!high:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	cmp #PLAYER_MOVE_SPEED
	bcc !underflow+
	sec
	sbc #PLAYER_MOVE_SPEED
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	jmp !end+

	// Here is low byte case:
	!low:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	cmp #PLAYER_MIN_POS
	bcc !end+ // don't allow to move off screen to left (bcc is A < value check)
	sec
	sbc #PLAYER_MOVE_SPEED
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	cmp #(SCREEN_EXIT_LEFT + 80)
	bcs !skip_scroll+
	lda REG_GAME_FINISH
	bne !skip_scroll+
	jsr scroll_map_right
	!skip_scroll:
	jmp !end+

	!underflow:
	lda #255
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(~((1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY) | (1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR)))
	sta REG_SPRITE_H

	!end:

	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_LEFT
	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_LEFT
	and #(~PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_RIGHT)
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES

	and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED
	beq !skip+

}

.macro player_update_vertical() {
	// Remove grounded and jump release flag:
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	and #(~PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_JUMP_ALLOWED)
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES

	lda REG_PLAYER_JUMP
	cmp #0
	bne !skip+
	jmp !falling+
	!skip:

	// jumping:
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, 0, 0, true, false)
	cmp #208 // character codes after 208 will be accepted as true collisions
	bcs !stop_jump+ // if A >= 208 -> stop jump
	lda REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sec
	sbc #PLAYER_JUMP_SPEED
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	dec REG_PLAYER_JUMP
	jmp !update_vertical_end+

	!stop_jump:
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_CRATE
	bne !+
	tax
	lda #BLOCK_ID_CRATE_BREAKING
	sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
	txa
	!:
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_CRATE_BREAKING
	bne !+
	lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
	sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
	!:
	lda #0
	sta REG_PLAYER_JUMP
	jsr sound_hit
	jmp !update_vertical_end+

	!falling:

	// // Print collision:
	// lda REG_GAME_SPRITE_BACKGROUND_COLLISION
	// and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY)
	// lsr
	// lsr
	// clc
	// adc #48
	// sta REG_SCREEN+240

	// Check exact screen character under sprite:
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, 0, 21, true, false)
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_SPRING // spring
	bne !skip_spring+
	tax
	lda #PLAYER_SPRING_JUMP_TIME
	sta REG_PLAYER_JUMP
	jsr sound_bounce
	txa
	!skip_spring:
	cmp #160 // character codes after 160 will be accepted as true collisions
	bcs !set_grounded+ // if A >= 160 -> set grounded
	// // DEBUG CHAR COORD
	// lda #0
	// sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y

	!not_grounded:
	lda REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	clc
	adc #PLAYER_FALL_SPEED
	cmp #250
	bcs !+
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	!:
	bcc !skip_die+
	lda REG_GAME_FINISH
	bne !skip_die+
	// Die when fallen out of screen:
	lda #0
	sta REG_PLAYER_HEALTH
	lda #250
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	jmp !set_grounded+
	!skip_die:
	jmp !update_vertical_end+

	!set_grounded:
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_GROUNDED
	and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_RESET
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	{
		// Align sprite to charset:
		lda REG_SPRITE_Y + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY * 2
		sec
		sbc #(SCREEN_BORDER_Y_OFFSET - 21)
		and #%11111000
		clc
		adc #(SCREEN_BORDER_Y_OFFSET - 21)
		sta REG_SPRITE_Y + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY * 2
		sta REG_SPRITE_Y + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR * 2
	}
	input_up()
	bne !set_jump_release+
	jmp !update_vertical_end+

	!set_jump_release:
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_JUMP_RELEASED
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES

	!update_vertical_end:
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_RIGHT
	beq !else+
	jsr move_player_right
	!else:
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_MOVED_LEFT
	beq !else+
	!enter:
	jsr move_player_left
	!else:
}
.macro player_set_state(state) {
	lda REG_PLAYER_STATE
	cmp #state
	beq !skip+
	// Only change when prev different from requested:
	lda #state
	sta REG_PLAYER_STATE
	lda #0
	sta REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME
	!skip:
	player_remove_attribute(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_ANIM_WITHIN_LOOP_REGION)
}
.macro player_update_anim() {
	// Anim frame update:
	lda REG_GAME_FRAME_COUNTER
	ldx REG_PLAYER_STATE
	and animTableSlowdown,x // frame pacing logic
	bne !skip+
	inc REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME
	lda REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME
	cmp animTableFrameCount,x
	bne !skip+ // skip over reset
	lda animTableLoopBegin,x // apply looping
	sta REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME
	!skip:

	lda REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME
	cmp animTableLoopBegin,x
	bcc !skip+ // if REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME < animTableLoopBegin,x
	// If control reaches here, it means the current frame is within loop region, so we can transition from it
	player_set_attribute(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_ANIM_WITHIN_LOOP_REGION)
	!skip:

	lda animTableFrameStart,x

	// Add current frame offset to sprite data:
	clc
	adc REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME

	// Attributes (written without flipping offset):
	tax
	lda REG_SPRITE_ATTRIBUTES, x
	sta REG_SPRITE_COLOR + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY
	lda REG_SPRITE_ATTRIBUTES + 10, x
	sta REG_SPRITE_COLOR + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR
	txa

	// Add flipping offset if needed:
	lda REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY)
	beq !noadd+
	txa
	clc
	adc #SPRITE_SHEET_TOTAL_COUNT
	jmp !skip+
	!noadd:
	txa
	!skip:

	// Add sprite data chunk offset
	clc
	adc #((REG_SPRITE_DATA - VIC_BANK_BEGIN) / 64)

	// Body:
	sta REG_SPRITE_PTR + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY

	// Hair:
	clc
	adc #10
	sta REG_SPRITE_PTR + SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR

	// // Print frame counter:
	// lda REG_PLAYER_ANIM_FRAME
	// adc #48
	// sta REG_SCREEN+160

	// // Print state:
	// lda REG_PLAYER_STATE
	// adc #48
	// sta REG_SCREEN+200
}
.macro player_update() {
	player_update_anim()
	player_update_vertical()
	weapon_retrieve()

	// Invulnerability blinking:
	lda REG_PLAYER_INVULNERABILITY_TIMER
	cmp #0
	beq !skip+
	sec
	sbc #1
	sta REG_PLAYER_INVULNERABILITY_TIMER
	and #%00000010
	bne !hidden+
	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	ora #((1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY) | (1 <<SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR))
	sta REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	jmp !skip+
	!hidden:
	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	and #(~((1 << SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY) | (1 <<SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_HAIR)))
	sta REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	!skip:

	// Key pickup:
	sprite_sprite_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, SPRITE_ID_KEY_BLUE)
	bne !skip+
	sprite_disable(SPRITE_ID_KEY_BLUE)
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BLUE
	.if (ONLY_ONE_KEY_ALLOWED == 1)
	{
		and #(~PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_PURPLE) // lose other key
	}
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	jsr sound_pickup
	!skip:
	sprite_sprite_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, SPRITE_ID_KEY_PURPLE)
	bne !skip+
	sprite_disable(SPRITE_ID_KEY_PURPLE)
	lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	ora #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_PURPLE
	.if (ONLY_ONE_KEY_ALLOWED == 1)
	{
		and #(~PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BLUE) // lose other key
	}
	sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
	jsr sound_pickup
	!skip:

	// Bg pickups:
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, 0, 0, true, true)
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, 0, 10, true, true)
	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, 0, 17, true, true)

}

.macro weapon_hit() {

.macro weapon_update() {
	lda REG_CUTSCENE
	cmp #0
	beq !+
	jmp !exit_forced+
	!:

	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_WEAPON)
	bne !enter+
	jmp !exit+ // Note: branch jump had too long relative offset, that's why jmp is used instead
	!enter:

	sprite_bg_collision(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, 0, 16, false, false)
	tax // save collision status of weapon

	lda REG_WEAPON_PROPERTIES
	and #WEAPON_PROPERTY_FALLING
	beq !moving+

	// Falling:
	txa // restore weapon collision status
	cmp #160 // character codes after 160 will be accepted as true collisions
	bcs !skip+ // if A >= 160 -> skip falling (hit)
	lda REG_SCROLL_ATTRIBUTES // can't fall while scroll to avoid random falling while mem is overwritten
	bne !skip+
	lda REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_WEAPON
	clc
	adc #WEAPON_FALL_SPEED
	sta REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * SPRITE_ID_WEAPON
	!skip:
	jmp !exit+

	!moving:
	lda REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
	and #(1 << SPRITE_ID_WEAPON)
	bne !left+
	move_sprite_right(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, WEAPON_MOVE_SPEED)
	jmp !skip+
	!left:
	move_sprite_left(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, WEAPON_MOVE_SPEED)
	!skip:

	txa // restore weapon collision status
	cmp #160 // character codes after 160 will be accepted as true collisions
	bcc !exit+ // if A < 160 -> skip disable (exit)
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_BLUE
	beq !exit+
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_PURPLE
	beq !exit+
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_WHITE
	beq !exit+
	cmp #BLOCK_ID_BREAKABLE_ROCK
	bne !not_breakable_by_weapon+
	lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
	sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
	!not_breakable_by_weapon:
	weapon_hit()

	!exit:

	lda REG_WEAPON_PROPERTIES
	and #WEAPON_PROPERTY_FALLING
	bne !weapon_noanim+
	sprite_anim(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, REG_WEAPON_FRAME, WEAPON_FRAME_START, WEAPON_FRAME_COUNT, %00000111, true, true, false)
	jmp !exit+
	!weapon_noanim:
	sprite_set_frame(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON, WEAPON_FRAME_START)
	!exit:
	!exit_forced:
}
.macro weapon_retrieve() {
	lda REG_WEAPON_PROPERTIES
	and #WEAPON_PROPERTY_FALLING
	beq !exit+

	sprite_sprite_collision(SPRITE_ID_PLAYER_BODY, SPRITE_ID_WEAPON)
	bne !exit+

	lda REG_WEAPON_PROPERTIES
	and #(~WEAPON_PROPERTY_FALLING)
	sta REG_WEAPON_PROPERTIES
	sprite_disable(SPRITE_ID_WEAPON)
	jsr sound_pickup

	!exit:
}
.macro update_sprite_active(sprite_id) {
	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !next+

	lda REG_SPRITE_Y + sprite_id * 2
	cmp #SCREEN_EXIT_BOTTOM
	bcs !disable+ // disable when falls at bottom

	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !lo+

	// High byte, check right bounds
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + sprite_id * 2
	cmp #(SCREEN_EXIT_RIGHT - 256)
	bcs !disable+ // disable when moves off screen right (bcs is A >= value check)
	jmp !next+

	!lo:
	// Low byte, check left bounds
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + sprite_id * 2
	cmp #SCREEN_EXIT_LEFT
	bcc !disable+ // disable when moves off screen to left (bcc is A < value check)
	jmp !next+

	!disable:
	sprite_disable(sprite_id)

	!next:
}

	update_sprite_active(SPRITE_ID_ENEMY1)

	update_sprite_active(SPRITE_ID_ENEMY3)

	update_sprite_active(SPRITE_ID_KEY_PURPLE)

.macro move_sprite_right(sprite_id, speed) {
	// Check high bit:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !low+ // If and result is zero then high bit is not set, handle low byte case
	
	// Here is high-byte case:
	!high:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	clc
	adc #speed
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	jmp !end+

	// Here is low byte case:
	!low:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	cmp #(255 - speed)
	bcs !overflow+ // handle overflow	
	clc
	adc #speed
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	jmp !end+

	!overflow:
	lda #0
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	ora #(1 << sprite_id)
	sta REG_SPRITE_H

	!end:
}
.macro move_sprite_left(sprite_id, speed) {
	// Check high bit:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !low+ // If and result is zero then high bit is not set, handle low byte case
	
	// Here is high-byte case:
	!high:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	cmp #speed
	bcc !underflow+
	sec
	sbc #speed
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	jmp !end+

	// Here is low byte case:
	!low:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	sec
	sbc #speed
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	jmp !end+

	!underflow:
	lda #255
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(~(1 << sprite_id))
	sta REG_SPRITE_H

	!end:
}
.macro wrap_sprite_hiposaware(sprite_id) {
	// Check high bit:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !low+ // If and result is zero then high bit is not set, handle low byte case
	
	// Here is high-byte case:
	!high:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	cmp #(350 - 255)
	bcc !end+
	// wrap at right:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(~(1 << sprite_id))
	sta REG_SPRITE_H
	lda #10
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	jmp !end+

	// Here is low byte case:
	!low:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id
	cmp #10
	bcs !end+
	// wrap at left:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	ora #(1 << sprite_id)
	sta REG_SPRITE_H
	lda #(320 - 255)
	sta REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id

	!end:
}

.macro sprite_set_frame(sprite_id, frame) {

	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !noflip+
	// flip:
	txa
	clc
	adc #SPRITE_SHEET_TOTAL_COUNT
	jmp !skip+
	!noflip:
	txa

.macro sprite_anim(sprite_id, anim_reg, framestart, framecount, slowdown, looped, pingpong, framestart_reg) {
	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !end+

	lda REG_GAME_FRAME_COUNTER
	and #slowdown // frame pacing logic
	bne !skip+

	.if (looped) {
		.if (pingpong) {
			lda anim_reg
			and #SPRITE_PINGPONG_BIT // check sign bit
			bne !neg+

			// no bit, increasing frames
			inc anim_reg
			lda anim_reg
			and #$0F
			cmp #(framecount - 1)
			bne !ovr+
			lda anim_reg
			ora #SPRITE_PINGPONG_BIT // set negative bit
			sta anim_reg
			jmp !ovr+

			!neg:
			// 1 bit, decreasing frames
			dec anim_reg
			lda anim_reg
			and #$0F
			cmp #0
			bne !ovr+
			sta anim_reg // negative bit already removed in prev check
			!ovr:
		}
		else {
			inc anim_reg
			lda anim_reg
			and #$0F
			cmp #framecount
			bne !ovr+
			lda #0
			sta anim_reg
			!ovr:
		}
	}
	else {
		inc anim_reg
		lda anim_reg
		and #$0F
		cmp #framecount
		bne !ovr+
		// disable sprite when reached frame count and not looped:
		lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
		and #(~(1 << sprite_id))
		sta REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
		!ovr:
	}

	!skip:

	// Update sprite ptr:
	lda anim_reg
	and #$0F
	clc
	.if(framestart_reg){
		adc #((REG_SPRITE_DATA - VIC_BANK_BEGIN) / 64)
		adc framestart
	}
	else{
		adc #((REG_SPRITE_DATA - VIC_BANK_BEGIN) / 64 + framestart)
	}
	tax
	lda REG_SPRITE_FLIPPED
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !noflip+
	// flip:
	txa
	clc
	adc #SPRITE_SHEET_TOTAL_COUNT
	jmp !skip+
	!noflip:
	txa
	!skip:
	sta REG_SPRITE_PTR + sprite_id

	// Update sprite attributes:
	.if(framestart_reg){
		ldx framestart
		lda REG_SPRITE_ATTRIBUTES,x
	}
	else{
		lda REG_SPRITE_ATTRIBUTES + framestart
	}
	sta REG_SPRITE_COLOR + sprite_id

	!end:
}

.macro sprite_sprite_collision(sprite_id_0, sprite_id_1) {
	lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
	and #((1 << sprite_id_0) | (1 << sprite_id_1))
	cmp #((1 << sprite_id_0) | (1 << sprite_id_1))
	bne !return_false+

	lda REG_GAME_SPRITE_SPRITE_COLLISION
	and #((1 << sprite_id_0) | (1 << sprite_id_1))
	cmp #((1 << sprite_id_0) | (1 << sprite_id_1))
	beq !precise_check+
	jmp !return_false+

	!precise_check:
	// Need to check that the two sprites collide exactly with each other, by distance check:

	// Check Y axis:
	abs_difference(REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * sprite_id_0, REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * sprite_id_1)
	cmp #22
	bcs !return_false+ // if A >= 22 -> return false

	// Check X axis:
	abs_difference(REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id_0, REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id_1)
	cmp #24
	bcs !return_false+ // if A >= 24 -> return false

	// return true:
	lda #0
	jmp !return+

	!return_false:
	lda #1

	!return:
}
.macro sprite_bg_collision(sprite_id, offsetX, offsetY, is_player, is_player_pickup) {

	.if(BACKGROUND_COLLISION_PRECISE == 1){
		// Check sprite visibility, skip hw sprite collision if disabled (invisible sprite still collides but not pixel perfect)
		lda REG_SPRITE_ENABLE
		and #(1 << sprite_id)
		beq !read_screen_mem+

		// Check hardware sprite-bg collision (this makes it pixel perfect):
		lda REG_GAME_SPRITE_BACKGROUND_COLLISION
		and #(1 << sprite_id)
		bne !read_screen_mem+
		lda #32 // return empty char
		jmp !return+

		!read_screen_mem:
	}

	// sprite vertical pos:
	lda REG_SPRITE_Y + 2 * sprite_id

	sec
	sbc #(SCREEN_BORDER_Y_OFFSET - offsetY)
	clc

	lsr // a/2
	lsr // a/4
	lsr // a/8
	
	// screen row ptr:
	tax
	lda screenRowStartAddressesLo,x
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_LO
	lda screenRowStartAddressesHi,x
	sta REG_GAME_TEMP_HI

	// check hi-pos:
	lda REG_SPRITE_H
	and #(1 << sprite_id)
	beq !lo_pos+

	// HI pos:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id

	clc
	adc #(SPRITE_PIXEL_WIDTH / 2)

	sec
	sbc REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL

	.if(offsetX < 0) {
		sec
		sbc #(-offsetX)
	}
	.if(offsetX > 0) {
		clc
		adc #(offsetX)
	}

	lsr // a/2
	lsr // a/4
	lsr // a/8

	clc
	adc #((256 - SCREEN_BORDER_X_OFFSET) / 8)
	jmp !end_x+

	!lo_pos:
	// LO pos:
	lda REG_SPRITE_X + 2 * sprite_id

	sec
	sbc #(SCREEN_BORDER_X_OFFSET - SPRITE_PIXEL_WIDTH / 2)
	sbc REG_SCROLL_HORIZONTAL
	clc

	.if(offsetX < 0) {
		sec
		sbc #(-offsetX)
	}
	.if(offsetX > 0) {
		clc
		adc #offsetX
	}

	lsr // a/2
	lsr // a/4
	lsr // a/8

	!end_x:


	tay // transfer column offset to Y
	// Now screen ROW address is stored in REG_GAME_TEMP_LO and HI
	// Now check character at screen address:
	lda (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y // character at pos, y = offset by posX/8

	.if(is_player) {
		// Player specific block modifiers:
		tax

		cpx #BLOCK_ID_BLUE
		bne !skip_key+
		// has blue key:
		.if (OPEN_KEYS == 1) {
			lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
			jmp !return+
		}
		else {
			lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
			and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BLUE
			beq !skip_key+
			lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
			jmp !return+
		}
		!skip_key:

		cpx #BLOCK_ID_PURPLE
		bne !skip_key+
		// has purple key:
		.if (OPEN_KEYS == 1) {
			lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
			jmp !return+
		}
		else {
			lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
			and #PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_PURPLE
			beq !skip_key+
			lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
			jmp !return+
		}
		!skip_key:

		cpx #BLOCK_ID_WHITE
		bne !skip_key+
		// has purple key:
		.if (OPEN_KEYS == 1) {
			lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
			jmp !return+
		}
		else {
			lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
			and #(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BLUE | PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_PURPLE)
			bne !skip_key+
			lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
			jmp !return+
		}
		!skip_key:

		.if(offsetX == 0) {
			cpx #BLOCK_ID_GRASS1
			bne !+
			lda #BLOCK_ID_GRASS_PUSHED1
			sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
			!:
			cpx #BLOCK_ID_GRASS2
			bne !+
			lda #BLOCK_ID_GRASS_PUSHED2
			sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
			!:
		}
	}

	.if (is_player_pickup) {
		// Key reset:
		cpx #BLOCK_ID_RESET
		bne !skip_key+
		lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
		and #(~(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BLUE | PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_PURPLE))
		sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
		!skip_key:

		// Key reset:
		cpx #BLOCK_ID_RESET_HORIZONTAL
		bne !skip_key+
		lda REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
		and #(~(PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_BLUE | PLAYER_ATTRIBUTE_KEY_PURPLE))
		sta REG_PLAYER_ATTRIBUTES
		!skip_key:

		.if (offsetY > 16)
		{
			lda REG_PLAYER_STATE
			cmp #PLAYER_STATE_CROUCH
			bne !skip_all_coin+
		}

		// Coin pickup:
		cpx #BLOCK_ID_COIN
		bne !skip_coin+
		lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
		sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
		lda REG_PLAYER_SCORE_LO
		clc
		adc #1
		sta REG_PLAYER_SCORE_LO
		update_hi_score()
		jsr sound_pickup
		!skip_coin:

		// Coin pickup:
		cpx #BLOCK_ID_COIN_LARGE
		bne !skip_coin+
		lda #BLOCK_ID_EMPTY
		sta (REG_GAME_TEMP_LO),y
		lda REG_PLAYER_SCORE_LO
		clc
		adc #10
		sta REG_PLAYER_SCORE_LO
		update_hi_score()
		jsr sound_pickup
		!skip_coin:

		!skip_all_coin:

		cpx #BLOCK_ID_FINISH
		bne !+
		lda REG_GAME_FINISH
		bne !+
		lda #23
		sta REG_GAME_FINISH
		!:
	}

	.if(is_player || is_player_pickup) {
		txa
	}

	!return:
}
